condition.name: HIV
condition.description: Antiretroviral medicines for HIV treatment and prevention (PrEP).

data.description: First long-acting injectable for HIV prevention (PrEP).
Protease inhibitor for treatment-experienced patients with PI resistance.

data.genericName: efavirenz, emtricitabine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
data.description: The first complete once-daily single-tablet HIV regimen (2006).
data.notes: Brand discontinued; generics may still be available.

data.description: Complete once-daily single-tablet regimen; among the most prescribed HIV medicines in the US.
Two-drug single-tablet regimen for virologically suppressed adults, including those switching from complex regimens.
data.notes: New in 2026. Starts with a 2-day initiation that adds Sunlenca tablets.

data.description: First complete long-acting injectable HIV treatment regimen.
Two-NRTI backbone pill, taken with a third drug.
One of the first fixed-dose HIV combination pills.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; generics may still be available.

data.genericName: emtricitabine, rilpivirine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
data.description: Complete rilpivirine-based single-tablet regimen (TDF version).

data.genericName: doravirine, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
data.description: Complete doravirine-based single-tablet regimen.
Two-NRTI backbone for treatment; also approved as daily oral PrEP.
data.notes: PrEP indication excludes people at risk through receptive vaginal sex.

data.description: Two-drug complete single-tablet regimen.
Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor; also used as oral lead-in for Cabenuva.
Pediatric dispersible formulation of rilpivirine.
data.notes: Listed as available by NIH HIVinfo (Sep 2026) but as discontinued by NYSDOH hivguidelines.org — verify before publishing.

data.description: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor; also a component of many combination pills.
Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor widely used in combination regimens.
Two-NRTI backbone pill, taken with a third drug.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; generics may still be available.

data.description: Atazanavir pre-boosted with cobicistat; taken with other HIV medicines.
The first fusion inhibitor; blocks HIV from fusing with the CD4 cell membrane.
data.notes: Brand discontinued.

data.genericName: elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide
data.description: Complete single-tablet regimen; the first approved with tenofovir alafenamide (TAF).
Two-drug single-tablet regimen for virologically suppressed adults switching therapy.
data.notes: New in 2026. Islatravir is a next-generation nucleoside reverse transcriptase translocation inhibitor (NRTTI).

data.description: Second-generation NNRTI, mainly for treatment-experienced patients.
The first FDA-approved integrase inhibitor.
High-dose raltegravir allowing once-daily dosing.
First two-drug complete regimen; for virologically suppressed adults switching therapy.
Co-formulated, pre-boosted protease inhibitor; taken with other HIV medicines.
Prodrug of the protease inhibitor amprenavir.
data.notes: Brand discontinued.

data.description: Protease inhibitor now used almost only as a pharmacokinetic booster for other PIs.
data.notes: Per HHS guidelines, used as a PK enhancer rather than as an active antiretroviral.

data.description: Complete rilpivirine-based single-tablet regimen; one of the smallest HIV pills.
Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used in combination regimens.
Darunavir pre-boosted with cobicistat; taken with other HIV medicines.
Pediatric-dose version of Prezcobix.
data.notes: New in 2026.

data.dosingFrequency: Once or twice daily (with food and a booster)
data.description: Protease inhibitor with a high barrier to resistance; must be boosted.
The first FDA-approved HIV medicine (1987).
data.notes: Also used to reduce perinatal (mother-to-child) transmission.

data.description: Protease inhibitor, usually given with a booster (ritonavir or cobicistat).
First-in-class attachment inhibitor for heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.
Blocks the CCR5 co-receptor HIV uses to enter cells.
data.notes: Requires a tropism test to confirm CCR5-tropic virus.

data.genericName: elvitegravir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
data.description: First integrase-inhibitor-based complete single-tablet regimen.
First-in-class capsid inhibitor for heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.
Non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; generic efavirenz may still be available.

data.genericName: efavirenz, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
data.description: Complete efavirenz-based single-tablet regimen (efavirenz 600 mg).

data.genericName: efavirenz, lamivudine, and tenofovir disoproxil fumarate
data.description: Lower-dose (efavirenz 400 mg) version of Symfi.
data.notes: Brand discontinued.

data.genericName: darunavir, cobicistat, emtricitabine, and tenofovir alafenamide
data.description: First darunavir-based complete single-tablet regimen.

data.dosingFrequency: Once daily (twice daily in some cases)
data.description: Integrase inhibitor with a high barrier to resistance; a core of many first-line regimens.
Pediatric dispersible formulation of dolutegravir.
Complete single-tablet regimen built on dolutegravir.
data.notes: HLA-B*5701 screening required (contains abacavir).

data.description: Pediatric dispersible version of Triumeq.
Triple-NRTI pill.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; triple-NRTI regimens are no longer recommended.

data.description: Monoclonal antibody for heavily treatment-experienced adults with multidrug-resistant HIV.
Two-NRTI backbone; in 2012 became the first medicine approved for HIV PrEP.
data.notes: Generic versions available.

data.description: Booster that raises blood levels of atazanavir or darunavir.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; cobicistat remains inside combination products.

data.description: Tenofovir alafenamide as a standalone tablet.
data.notes: Standalone Vemlidy is FDA-approved for chronic hepatitis B, not HIV; TAF is used for HIV inside combination products (e.g. Biktarvy, Descovy).

data.description: First-generation non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; generic nevirapine may still be available.

data.description: Extended-release, once-daily version of nevirapine.
data.notes: Brand discontinued; generics may still be available.

data.description: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor; also approved for chronic hepatitis B.
Oral cabotegravir used as an optional lead-in before Cabenuva or Apretude injections.
Twice-yearly injectable for HIV prevention (PrEP).
Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor used as part of a combination regimen.
data.notes: HLA-B*5701 screening required before starting (hypersensitivity risk).
